stages.desc: Private Morales has asked me to find and retrieve the corpse of her dead husband. His body is apparently being used as a lure to draw in NCR troops and slaughter them. Better keep a look out for traps and snipers...
The body is just east of REPCONN HQ and I should carry it to the troopers camped out on the north side of the railroad tracks.
I managed to get Ranger Morales' corpse away from the Fiends. I should return to Pvt. Morales and let her know her husband's body is safe.

notes: Though both Christina and one of the troopers at the barricade mention the death of Ranger Jackson, there is no reward for returning his body to the troopers; Jackson's body is near the rigged shotgun trap between two nearby buildings (sometimes the body may not spawn).
During the body retrieval, the trooper at the checkpoint will have unique dialogue if one brought the body back and either took significant damage or no damage at all.
Before completing the quest, troopers at Camp McCarran can be heard complaining about the NCR not retrieving the body and how it affects Pvt. Morales.
After completing the quest, Mr. New Vegas can be heard over Radio New Vegas making a report about the heroic deed and Christina Morales' gratitude.
Knocking a Fiend sniper off the roof onto the landmines placed around Ranger Morales' body does not appear to set them off.

notes: Due to Sexton not being a marked target during We Are Legion, it is possible to continue bringing him Legion ears even after killing off the camp's officers.

Various Legionaries – including those at the Fort, the Legate's camp, members of Legionary assassin squads, and the three waves that attack Bitter Springs during I Forgot to Remember to Forget – do not drop ears upon death during this quest. For this reason, it is advisable to speak to Pvt. Sexton and start this quest prior to completing Restoring Hope, in order to maximize one's "ear harvesting" opportunities.

The number of ears collected will be represented as tally marks in the mess hall to Sexton's right, beneath a bull with the initials of Caesar's Legion above it, but only in multiples of 5 (e.g. at 11-14 ears, only 10 marks are shown). If one has not progressed far enough, the station will still be occupied and there will be no option to confirm this with Andy. Upon receiving the task to check on the station, the script that wipes out the station will be triggered when next entering the station interior.

When inside the station with the dead NCR troopers, there is a frag mine under each of the two bodies in the first room and a tripwire behind a closed door, linked to a rigged shotgun beneath a bunkbed, rigged to cause a bottlecap mine to detonate two explosive canisters.

Quick walkthrough.text: Unmarked Quest: Arizona Scavenger
Reach Cottonwood Cove and speak with Aurelius of Phoenix at or in the HQ building;; agree to collect proof of NCR kills to aid the Legion.

Pickpocket/collect NCR dogtags from NCR troopers and Rangers and return them to Aurelius;; pass a 35 Barter skill check to persuade him to allow Decanus Severus to trade dogtags for ammo and supplies.
Reward: Legion fame; Caps or assorted ammunition and items

notes: The NCR troopers found at some associated locations (such as Camp Golf) are known to respawn every 3-4 game days, allowing one to theoretically collect infinite NCR dogtags, Legion fame, and ammo and supplies (if trading with Severus) through this quest.
NCR dogtags can be pickpocketed from the drunk troopers found wandering around the Strip.

Prior to being patched, one could kill the injured soldiers scattered throughout the no-man's-land between Nelson and Camp Forlorn Hope and retrieve their dogtags to gain Legion fame without a Karma or NCR reputation loss. Beware of frag mines placed near or under their bodies as traps. Injured soldiers will respawn every three in-game days.
Mister Sandman kills can also be performed without a Karma or NCR reputation loss.
When trading with Severus, the most profitable item to gain from him is the 10mm SMG, having a dogtag-to-cap ratio of 1:79.

Due to several bugs with Decanus Severus' dialog, the fastest way to accumulate Legion fame is to turn in tags for food, five at a time. This nets +12 to Legion fame for every 5 tags turned in, with 100 fame granting the highest possible positive reputation.

If one is Vilified with the Legion, but not yet started Render Unto Caesar by receiving the Mark of Caesar, it is still possible to start this quest. Initially, if one asks for supplies in trade for dogtags, they won't be able to get them, as Decanus Severus will not engage in dialogue; in this case, one can still trade in dogtags to Aurelius for caps and Legion fame. One will be required to wear faction armor in order to engage Severus in conversation and access his rewards.

For the former, when the player character reaches a chips threshold while gambling, a Jackpot sound will be heard and they automatically receive the prize(s), while the latter has a generic White Glove comes to the player character to reward them.

The Sierra Madre's casino uses holograms as table managers; since the holograms do not talk to the player character, the award is automatically given once choosing the relevant "dialogue" option, and one will instead get a notification about the prize winnings and the eventual permanent ban.
Winning the maximum and receiving the permanent ban at all three casinos on the Strip during their associated quests will unlock the "The Courier Who Broke the Bank" achievement/trophy.

If one wants to win the renewable supply of complimentary vouchers from the Sierra Madre casino, it is advisable to begin gambling as soon as the casino is available during Put the Beast Down, since as soon as one leaves the Sierra Madre to return to the Mojave Wasteland after finishing the Dead Money add-on, it is normally impossible to return again.

Quick walkthrough.text: Unmarked Quest: Bounty Killer
Reach Camp McCarran and speak with Colonel James Hsu;; ask about the camp's problems with the Fiends.
Agree to help the NCR by assassinating Motor-Runner in Vault 3.
Reach Vault 3 in the South Vegas ruins south-southwest of Camp McCarran.
(Optional) Locate and speak with the injured Ranger Bryce Anders in the living quarters.
Offer to use a doctor's bag to heal him.
Attack and kill him or; pass a 75 Speech skill check to convince him to attack Motor-Runner immediately.
Karma loss
Pass a 75 Speech check to recruit him as a temporary companion or; choose dialogue options to convince him to return to McCarran.
Enter the maintenance section, kill Motor-Runner and obtain Motor-Runner's helmet.
Return to Col. Hsu.
Reward: NCR fame (increased if Anders left alive); 300 caps

notes: Bryce Anders will die if he takes any non-zero amount of damage, regardless of what conversation options have been used to get him moving; this is due to him being scripted that if he is hurt by a member of the Fiends he dies instantly. This was done to ensure his death if chosen to send him in alone, but the effect remains active indefinitely even after he leaves the Vault if convinced. To keep him alive, it is best to either send him back to base or clean out the whole vault prior to enlisting his aid with Motor-Runner.

He can also be killed by Fiends in the entrance area of the vault after meeting him and tell him to wait. It appears that although there is a wall between the room where Bryce stays and the entrance area, the Fiends can actually shoot 'through' the wall. Thus it is important to clear the Fiends as quickly as possible if one wants him to survive.

If one has not yet started Aba Daba Honeymoon (and wants to at some point) it is recommended to refrain from entering the maintenance wing with Motor-Runner due to a bug with Motor-Runner that causes him to initiate his dialogue options only once. Thus it is advisable to trigger Aba Daba Honeymoon with Diane first and advance it to the point of delivering the package to Motor-Runner, otherwise that quest may fail.

Conversely, upon killing Motor-Runner, if Aba Daba Honeymoon was not completed beforehand, it will immediately be marked as failed. This can be solved by completing the parts of that quest that require Motor-Runner alive before accepting this quest. Once that is done, he is fair game. Alternatively, faking Motor-Runner's death by merely acquiring his helmet from pickpocketing will avoid the need to kill him.

If one kills Motor-Runner before starting this quest, Anders may appear at the vault entrance (in the Wasteland) and will begin walking back to Camp McCarran. This may also occur if one takes Motor-Runner's helmet to claim the bounty and leaves him alive.
Colonel Hsu may give thanks for saving Anders even if the player hasn't met him.

If one has previously entered Vault 3 wearing Great Khan armor during Aba Daba Honeymoon, the Fiends will not be hostile the next time one enters even if they are not wearing the outfit. Upon killing Motor-Runner, only the Fiends in the adjacent area will become hostile, not the entire Vault.

Quick walkthrough.text: Unmarked Quest: Dealing with Contreras
Reach Camp McCarran and speak with either Lt. Boyd in the terminal building or Sgt. Contreras in the supply shack; Note: Must be Level ≥12 to work with Contreras.
Agree to help Lt. Boyd find evidence of Contreras' illicit dealings.
Pass a 50 Speech/Barter skill check to convince Contreras to accept help.
Locate the supply database terminal in the supply shack and hack the Average-level lock to acquire Contreras' weapons manifest.
Speak with Isaac outside the Gun Runners kiosk near Freeside's east gate.
Return to Boyd and give her the manifest.
Return to Contreras.
Pass an 80 Speech/Barter check or; obtain 100 pieces of junk metal (e.g. tin cans, hot plates, scrap metal, etc.) to finalize the arms deal with the Gun Runners.
Obtain the medical supplies from Blake at the Crimson Caravan Company compound;; pass a 25 Science/Medicine check to point out the supplies' viability as drug components.
Reach Miguel's Pawn Shop in Westside and speak with Keller.
Pass a 7 Perception + Intelligence attribute check to expose Keller as a Ranger;; pass a hidden 70 Speech check to convince Keller not to arrest them.
Inform Contreras about Keller.
Give Keller the medical supplies as proof of Contreras' illicit dealings;; pass a 60 Speech skill check / 7 Charisma attribute check to convince Keller they are not an accomplice
Agree to kill Keller or; pass an 80 Speech / 60 Barter check to convince Keller to partner with Contreras, then an 80 Speech / 70 Barter check to convince Contreras to partner with Keller.
Reward: NCR fame; This Machine
Reward: 80 XP
Reward: Access to Contreras' full vendor inventory; This Machine; 150 caps (50 Barter)

notes: The quest name is a play on words, with the dual meaning of "dealing" with Contreras being where one either "deals" with him by keeping his supply line intact for their access or "deals" with him by turning him in and cutting off his supply line.
If talking to Contreras does not initiate the quest, the weapons manifest can still be downloaded from his terminal to report his activity to Lt. Boyd to complete her part of the quest.

After acquiring the medical supplies, one can find them in the inventory and use them like an aid item. This will function the same way as a doctor's bag but will limit the options for completing the quest.

Siding with Keller and performing the multiple Speech / Barter checks retains the choice of turning Contreras in to Boyd, getting This Machine, but resulting in the same outcome as siding with Boyd (Contreras is imprisoned, and his stock is limited.)
If a companion kills Keller, NCR reputation will not be affected.
If Isaac died during/before this quest, it will be impossible to side with Contreras.

By choosing the dialogue option for combat with Keller, he can be lured outside the pawn shop. After he loses track, use a Stealth Boy. Follow him inside and make the kill with a stealthy weapon to avoid gaining NCR infamy.

Keller can be sided with for the XP, then Contreras killed while hidden and his body looted for his caps including what was sold to him. Additionally, hacking his terminal and giving the evidence to Boyd will still grant This Machine.
After downloading the manifest and discreetly killing Contreras, Boyd still awards the player character with This Machine as if nothing changed. Afterward, his corpse will appear in the prison cell.

Taking a picture of the stone with the Codac R9000 given by Michael Angelo during Classic Inspiration will cause Kowalski to react as if it was shot with a firearm. This is because the R9000 is coded as a ranged weapon, and fires invisible projectiles that normally don't anger NPCs.

After each fight, all of the player character's items are returned to their inventory all at once, but each item has its own on-screen pop-up message. These messages can take several minutes to clear. To avoid this, simply save the game after a fight and reload; this will cancel the pop-ups.

During this quest, the check for the player character's sex in the game files occurs upon selecting the dialogue option with Otho to ask about fighting in the arena. Barring any other ill effects, it is possible for a female Courier to use the sex change console command and access these gladiatorial match dialogue options before switching back.

It is possible for the Mysterious Stranger to appear and kill opponents in the arena, even though the Courier is supposed to kill all opponents themselves. Otho and other nearby NPCs will not acknowledge this, and nobody will turn hostile for inadvertently breaking the rules.

notes: The timer to make Lily play her holotape is set on the first time that the player enters the sleep/wait menu after fulfilling the three conditions. Furthermore, the timer works by taking a float value fRestTimer based on the exact time that that sleep/wait menu is activated, and then playing the holotape once the current time of day becomes greater than the value of fRestTimer. Since Fallout: New Vegas uses a 24-hour clock, this means that a player who chooses to wait for an hour at 23:30 will not be able to hear the recording at least until 23:31 on the following game day. This can make the recording very hard to trigger without knowing exactly what time the timer was set to.

Thus, once the three dialogue conditions are fulfilled, not entering the sleep or wait menu until after midnight (when the time value resets to 0) is the most reliable way to make sure the recording will play.
Since it is not possible to sleep or wait to let the time pass, another method to trigger the event is to fast travel to different locations to make the time pass faster.

notes: Getting a tip from Rotface will not actually trigger any quests related to them, nor provide a map marker to where the quest-giver is located.

When entering Freeside after buying 11 tips, Rotface will now be wearing Eulogy Jones' hat. Due to the way his script is set up, this can only happen upon purchasing exactly 11 tips; if any more tips are bought, the script to give him the hat will not trigger. As such, the most reliable way to get him the hat is to pay for exactly 11 tips, then wait outside the east gate in the Mojave Wasteland, then re-enter Freeside, whereupon he should be wearing the new hat. The hat, which appears to be an expensive cowboy hat with a purple feather, can be obtained by killing or reverse-pickpocketing Rotface - killing Rotface does not cause a drop in Karma, nor will it cause Freeside infamy or hostility from the local residents.

In cut content, this quest had various potential outcomes. The Courier had the option to tell Rotface that his hat looked nice; the next time they returned, Rotface would be wearing Eulogy Jones' suit, and would ask the Courier's opinion on his investment. Based on the response, Rotface would have different reactions the next time he was talked to; he would either buy a .357 Magnum revolver and attempt to mug the Courier, leave Freeside to seek his fortune, join the Followers, or be murdered by a Freeside thug for his newfound wealth.

infobox.reward: Discounted services from Ada Straus

Purchase all of her medical services in one conversation.

notes: Gaining a positive reputation with Novac will earn an additional discount on Straus' goods and services.
Due to the mentioned bug below, this is now the only means to get discounted services from her.

Pass the 2,000-caps credit check or; pass an 80 Science skill check or; acquire a counterfeit passport from Ralph during Papers, Please

infobox.reward: Strip fame; Well Rested bonus; Discounted/free purchase of Vault 21 hotel room (player-dependent)

Quick walkthrough.text: Unmarked quest: Suits You, Sarah
Reach Vault 21 on the Strip and speak with Sarah Weintraub;; ask about what items are sold in the gift shop.
Agree to acquire authentic Vault jumpsuits for Sarah from the Mojave's various Vaults including Vaults 3, 11, 19, 22, and 34.
Return and give the jumpsuits to Sarah.
Reward: Strip fame; Well Rested bonus; Discounted/free purchase of Vault 21 hotel room (player-dependent)

notes: Giving Sarah one jumpsuit at a time results in more Strip fame than giving all 30 jumpsuits at once due to the fame being rewarded every time the delivery dialogue option is selected rather than how many jumpsuits are given. I.e., selling 1 jumpsuit 30 times nets +30 Strip fame in contrast to 15 jumpsuits 2 times which nets +2 Strip fame.

For the first visit, Sarah will accept 10 suit offers in succession. After this, walking near either doorway of the gift shop will re-trigger an inventory check enabling selling more suits. Waiting or leaving the gift shop is not necessary.

There is no limit to how many times the player character can sleep with Sarah for the Well Rested bonus, but in Hardcore mode, it does not lower the sleep meter and simply passes time. This makes it necessary to rest normally in one of the beds, which also passes time, leading to dehydration and starvation.

Passing the Barter check with Sarah to receive payment for Boomer clothing will earn caps, but they will not count towards the total number of Vault jumpsuits that must be given to her in order to unlock the dialogue to have sex with her.

If the player character is female, the two speech checks will not show up, even after the quest has been completed. Renting a room is not required prior to sleeping with Sarah. The game will simply recognize that the quest has been completed and the option to sleep with her will be automatic.

infobox.reward: 2 caps per dogtag turned in; NCR fame100 caps + 6 beers; OR; Karma gain

Quick walkthrough.text: Unmarked Quest: Tags of Our Fallen
Reach Camp Forlorn Hope and speak with Quartermaster Mayes;; ask about the state of the camp.
Agree to find and return any NCR dogtags for Mayes.
Return a total of 15 dogtags to Mayes.
Reward: 2 caps per dogtag turned in; NCR fame100 caps + 6 beer; OR; Karma gain

notes: Mayes will not accept the irradiated NCR dogtags found on the feral trooper ghouls encountered in Camp Searchlight during We Will All Go Together - those are to be given to First Sergeant Astor during that quest.

The payout from Mayes for turned-in NCR dogtags is comparatively lower than that offered by Aurelius of Phoenix during Arizona Scavenger, who pays 10 bottle caps per dogtag; passing a 35 Barter check will even allow Decanus Severus to accept dogtags in exchange for ammunition and other supplies. The main difference is that the Courier will garner Legion fame for turning them in to Aurelius of Phoenix or Decanus Severus (though this will not incur NCR infamy).

infobox.reward: 75 caps; 10 brahmin steaks (from the McBride house fridge); Novac fame

Quick walkthrough.text: Unmarked quest: The Screams of Brahmin
Reach Novac and speak with either Jeannie May Crawford or No-bark Noonan;; ask about ongoing events around the town.
Speak with Dusty McBride at his ranch;; agree to find out the cause of his brahmin dying.
Locate and kill the stealthy nightkin near the McBride ranch, then recover the holotape on its body;; (optional) wait until around midnight for it to appear.
Return to Dusty.
Reward: 75 caps; 10 brahmin steaks (from the McBridge house fridge); Novac fame

notes: At higher levels, the attacker may instead be a stronger nightkin master.
If Dusty McBride is killed before completing the quest, the nightkin can still be killed, but no cap or karma reward can be obtained.
If one remains undetected close to the nightkin without attacking, he will occasionally make unique comments including ones that vary depending on the player character's current active companion.
"Horns will help the bull. Voices say they knew that would happen." (Great Khans and Caesar's Legion)
"Bears in pain. Head voices not surprised." (NCR)
"Ha ha. Funny robot make blinky sounds." (ED-E)
"Head voices say smart man also metal man. Don't like metal men." (Arcade Gannon)
"Book girl has hard decision to make." (Veronica Santangelo)
"Head voices say quiet man knows more than he says about horns." (Craig Boone)
"Head voices say they knew flower girl's father." (Rose of Sharon Cassidy)
"Head voices know smelly ghoul. He old and good with guns." (Raul Tejada)
"Head voices speak of doggy with squishy brain." (Rex)
"Head voices say someone close. Someone like us." (Lily Bowen)

infobox.reward: 2-9 Sunset Sarsaparilla star bottle caps (player-dependent); Various loot from one or both NPCs

Quick walkthrough.text: Unmarked Quest: The Star Showdown
Obtain at least one Sunset Sarsaparilla star bottle cap, then travel to Nipton going east from the Nipton Road pit stop.;; witness the gunfight between Tomas and Jacklyn or intervene.
Speak with the survivor about the attack and its cause.
Tomas lives
Jacklyn lives
Leave him alone or; demand his "lucky star" necklace or; pass a 40 Speech skill check to receive it peacefully.
Leave her alone or; comment on her collecting star bottle caps or; pass a 7 Intelligence check to callout her theft of the caps from Tomas.
Reward: 2-9 Sunset Sarsaparilla star bottle caps (player-dependent); Various loot from one or both NPCs

notes: If the player character does not actually pass the area in which they have the gunfight, they may be randomly approached by either of them later in the game.
If the fight is missed, he will normally walk to the Courier and if his bottle caps were not taken by the Courier, one can find him at the place where the gunfight was.
Tomas and Jacklyn have a special faction tag that causes random critters and raiders to ignore them, to prevent randomly spawned mobs from interrupting their gunfight.
Tomas and Jacklyn both have relatively high HP (120 each) and a severely low Guns skill level (5 each), so their shootout may last a significant period of time until one dies if left alone.

After speaking with the Courier (if they do not become hostile), the survivor of the gunfight will travel to the Mojave Outpost and disappear from the game world, taking their amount of star bottle caps with them.

If the Courier has gained the Terrifying Presence perk, it is possible to get as many as 16 Sunset Sarsaparilla star bottle caps from this encounter. To accomplish this, Jacklyn must win the fight, and the ensuing conversation must be ended without provoking her to attack or betray the Courier. Jacklyn's 9 star bottle caps can then be pickpocketed off of her as she walks away. Then take Tomas's journal from his body to prove her a liar. Reinitiate conversation after doing so, accuse her of stealing, and then demand the necklace with the Terrifying Presence option. She will hand over seven additional bottle caps before walking back to the Mojave Outpost and disappearing.

infobox.reward: Goodsprings fame; 50 - 75 caps; 10 - 35 XP

Quick walkthrough.text: Unmarked Quest: Trudy's Radio Repair
Reach Goodsprings and speak with Trudy in the Prospector Saloon;; ask about her previous visitors during They Went That-a-Way.
Pass a 20 Repair check to fix the broken radio on the shelf behind Trudy's bar.
Return to Trudy;; pass a 20 Barter skill check to negotiate the caps reward from 50 to 75.
Reward: Goodsprings fame; 50 - 75 caps; 10 - 35 XP

notes: Despite Trudy mentioning her desire to hear Mr. New Vegas's voice again, when fixed, the radio is actually set to Mojave Music Radio without the DJ's narration.
Upon fixing the radio, Trudy will mention she was able to hear it functioning again even if she is outside the saloon at the time.

infobox.reward: 2,000 caps per snow globe (maximum 14,000); Delivered snow globes displayed in presidential suite

Quick walkthrough.text: Unmarked Quest: Useless Baubles or Fancy Trinkets?
Enter the Lucky 38 during The House Always Wins and speak with the securitron, Jane in the penthouse;; ask about Mr. House's collection of snow globes
Find and retrieve the 7 snow globes from locations around the Mojave Wasteland (see below), then bring them to Jane.
Reward: 2,000 caps per snow globe (maximum 14,000); Delivered snow globes displayed in presidential suite

notes: After the player character has returned seven snow globes from the Mojave Wasteland, the snow globe stand will "sparkle" for a moment.

If Mr. House is killed (either independently or as part of a non-House faction quest), Jane will disappear from the penthouse and it will no longer be possible to remove the snow globes from the inventory. However, PC users can use the console command to spawn Jane to their location to continue adding snow globes to the stand. Should Jane still be aggressive after spawning, use the console command after having talked to her to stop all combat.

page: We Must Stop Beating Like This

infobox.reward: Unique interaction with Victor
previous: Ain't That a Kick in the Head (quest)
related: We Must Stop Meeting Like This

Quick walkthrough.text: Unmarked Quest: We Must Stop Beating Like This
After completing Ain't That a Kick in the Head and before entering the Strip, enter combat near Goodsprings.
Speak with Victor.
Reward: Unique interaction with Victor

notes: Victor may frequently use his grenade launcher for combat. Since Victor only appears when the player character has ≤50% HP, the grenades could sometimes damage and/or kill the player character as well.

Victor will never spawn during combat with the Powder Gangers in Ghost Town Gunfight or with the geckos at Goodsprings source during Back in the Saddle; this is explicitly scripted by the quest so as not to happen.

Victor can and will spawn during Barton the Fink, whether during combat against the geckoes or during the ambush by Barton Thorn. Otherwise, the encounter is likely to occur during They Went That-a-Way.

If Victor was killed during this encounter, when meeting him again at relevant locations during They Went That-a-Way and/or We Must Stop Meeting Like This, there will be a unique dialogue option to comment on his previous "death."Victor: "Do I look destroyed, pardner? It's harder to put {{Tooltip|Old|{Ol} }} Vic in Boot Hill than you might think! I wouldn't be much use stuck inside just one Securitron! No, if the one I'm in turns up a goner, I just find another, fine as cream gravy!"; (Victor's dialogue)

page: We Must Stop Meeting Like This

infobox.reward: None
previous: Ain't That a Kick in the Head (quest)

Quick walkthrough.text: Unmarked Quest: We Must Stop Meeting Like This

After completing Ain't That a Kick in the Head and before entering the Lucky 38, speak with Victor as he appears in Goodsprings, Novac, Boulder City and the Strip during They Went That-a-Way and Ring-a-Ding-Ding!
Leads to: The House Always Wins

notes: After the final conversation on the Strip, Victor will disappear from the other locations in the Mojave Wasteland, only appearing outside and inside the Lucky 38 of which the latter has him as a required interaction to use the elevator (unless House is killed and The House Has Gone Bust! is failed which causes him to disappear from there as well).

It is possible to talk to the version of Victor right in front of the door to the Lucky 38 before talking to the version that spawns when entering the Strip for the first time. In this case, after exiting conversation with the doorman robot, the robot on the street will immediately start the dialogue to welcome their arrival to the Strip.

infobox.reward: Stealth Boy (optional)

Quick walkthrough.text: Unmarked Quest: Wind-Brahmin Wrangler
Reach the Brooks tumbleweed ranch north of the Griffin Wares sacked caravan; and enter the cattle pen on the north end.
Speak with the nightkin "merchant"
Pay him with "all" caps to buy a "wind-brahmin."
Refuse his offer.
Attack and kill the nightkin.
Reward: Stealth Boy (optional)

notes: The nightkin will retain the caps taken in their inventory, which become accessible upon death. Their Stealth Boy can also be taken at this point.
The nightkin comments that the noises he hears are just those of his "brahmin."

The "wind-brahmin" can be purchased for as low as 0 caps if the player deposits all their caps in a storage container before the interaction. As long as the player agrees to the purchase, the nightkin will not turn hostile no matter how little caps the player had, even if none.
The Stealth Boy can be pickpocketed from the nightkin with no Karma loss.

infobox.reward: Scribe Counter

Quick walkthrough.text: Unmarked Quest: You Make Me Feel Like a Woman
Reach the 188 Trading Post west of Boulder City and recruit Veronica as a companion;; ask about her personal life and the topic of her goals.
Acquire a fancy dress (must be formal wear or White Glove Society attire), then place it in Veronica's inventory.
Reward: Scribe Counter

notes: Due to scripting constraints, Veronica won't actually wear the dress she's given (characters wear whatever apparel in their inventory has the highest DT, and non-armored clothing like dresses generally have zero), but she will still thank the Courier if one is put in her inventory and says she will try it on later.
One can make Veronica wear her dress by placing it in her inventory and using the following console commands: to select her, then to remove her robes and to remove her hood.
